newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Telekom debt to fall - German banks.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Telekom debt to fall - German banks.

text.p: German telephone monopoly Deutsche Telekom could see its net debt fall significantly by the end of the century from its current level of 92.17 billion marks, two of Germany's top banks said on Friday.
A report by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, the research wing of Deutsche Bank, said that net debts at Deutsche Telekom would fall to 62.93 billion by the year 2000.
Meanwhile, a report by Commerzbank, Germany's third-largest bank, forecasts an annual reduction in debt of ten billion marks a year to around 60 billion marks by the end of the century.
Deutsche Telekom, Europe's biggest telecoms company, is due to be privatised in a 15-billion-mark flotation beginning on November 17, making it Europe's largest-ever public issue.
Deutsche Telekom's chief financial officer Joachim Kroeske said that the company will make up 4.5 percent of the total value of the DAX when it is floated.
Deutsche Bank is one of the main co-ordinators of the sell-off, while Commerzbank is a junior co-lead manager in the consortium organising the sale.

Debt levels at Telekom have been the focus of attention for many analysts. A recent report by the research wing of BZW Bank, not part of the consortium, ranked the group as the 24th-largest debtor in the world, just ahead of Turkey in 25th.
Telekom's main strengths lay in its highly-effective telephone service network, its cable television network and its mobile telephone business, Deutsche MG said.

Deutsche MG analysts go on to forecast a fall in sales in 1996 to an estimated 62.650 billion from 66.135 billion in 1995, rising to an estimated 66.489 billion marks in 1997 and 69.085 billion the year after.
Commerzbank also forecasts sales falling in 1996 to 62.316 billion marks, before rising to 67.177 billion marks in 1997 and 71.480 billion marks in 1998.
In terms of profits, Deutsche MG is forecasting net profit of 1.364 billion marks in 1996, rising to 4.444 billion marks in 1997 and to 8.303 billion marks the year after.
Commerzbank forecasts net profit of 1.493 billion marks in 1996, rising to 5.058 billion marks in 1997 and 6.429 billion marks in 1998.
Deutsche MG said: "According to our prognoses, costs and sales will slowly but surely rise," leading to slow growth in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation.
Deutsche MG regarded an issue price of between 20 and 30 marks as appropriate, based on its valuation of the company.
